key_insight: ParetoChat uses an LLM as a conversational bridge that turns natural-language preferences into multi-objective optimization parameters and iteratively steers the search toward Pareto-efficient solutions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical interface for decision support in operations research, reducing the burden on stakeholders to manually encode weights, priorities, or reference points.
method: Multi-agent LLM architecture separates input parsing, MCDM reasoning, solution presentation, and feedback handling.
Natural-language requests are translated into structured scalarization parameters for an underlying optimization solver.
The system iterates with the decision maker by proposing candidates and updating preferences from feedback.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates ParetoChat in simulation with an LLM-based decision-maker and on benchmark DESDEO methods, plus case studies on binary knapsack, set-partitioning, and courier-order assignment instances.
watch_item: Performance depends on the LLM correctly interpreting user intent, so ambiguous prompts or hallucinated preference translations could misguide optimization.
paper_title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization
